sections.html:
Raleigh County lies in southern West Virginia, with Beckley as its seat and its lone city. Census takers found 74,591 residents in 2020, and the 2025 estimate has slipped to 71,775 from a high of 96,273 in 1950. Coal drove that growth. Miners opened the seams in the 1890s, rails arrived in Beckley in 1901, and headcount leapt from 12,436 in 1900 to 25,633 in 1910.

The 1980s brought machines that replaced thousands of miners. Beckley coped better than the small camps, helped by its spot where Interstates 64 and 77 cross U.S. 19. Retail, services, tourism and hospitals carry the local economy now. Visitors come for the Exhibition Coal Mine, Grandview Park, Twin Falls State Park and the Winterplace ski resort, and part of New River Gorge National Park and Preserve lies inside the county line. Many sellers here own an older house, and plenty are heirs holding a property they never planned to manage.

Beyond Beckley you will find the towns of Lester, Mabscott and Sophia, and communities such as Shady Spring, Ghent and Piney View. Seven magisterial districts were merged into three in the 1970s. An old deed might name a district like Trap Hill that is no longer on any map, so hand that deed to the title company early.

Two desks share the work. Raleigh County's sheriff runs the Tax Division, which mails bills and takes money. The county assessor puts a value on each parcel and decides its class. A question about a ticket goes to the sheriff, and a question about your number goes to the assessor.

When staff runs thin, a satellite office may go dark for a day, so ring ahead before you head out to Ghent or Glen Daniel. Online payment and records links live on the Raleigh County Sheriff tax page and the Assessor's site.

Raleigh County bills in two halves. Sheriffs mail tickets on or after July 15, and the halves fall due on September 1 and March 1, the same calendar used statewide.

  • Pay the first half by September 1. It turns delinquent on October 1.
  • Pay the second half by March 1. It turns delinquent on April 1.
  • Paying ahead of either due date earns a 2.5 percent discount on that half.
  • Late tax picks up interest at 9 percent a year.

Leaving a ticket unpaid can end in a lien sale. West Virginia Code 11A-3-2 has the sheriff build a second list by September 10 of parcels that were still unpaid on September 1. The State Auditor receives those certified liens on October 31. Before certification, an owner clears the debt with the sheriff by paying the tax, the interest and the charges: $25 for the list plus $10 for every mailed notice. Once certified, the Auditor handles redemption.

sections.h2: How a Raleigh County house is assessed
sections.html:
The assessor values your property at 60 percent of market value. Your rate then turns on the class the parcel falls in. A home that the owner owns and lives in, plus an owner-occupied farm, is Class II. Other property outside a municipality is Class III, and other property inside one is Class IV. Compared with Class I, Class II pays double and Classes III and IV pay four times as much.

Rentals and vacant inherited houses do not meet the Class II test. Find out your parcel's class before you list, since the class sets the bill your buyer steps into.

On where the money goes, tax year 2024 levies in the county split this way: schools 67.1 percent, county purposes 27.7 percent, municipal purposes 4.8 percent and state purposes 0.4 percent. Owner-occupied homes carry about 42 percent of the real estate levy.

Appeals are made in person, and the clock is short. Every winter the assessor lays out real estate and personal property assessments for public inspection, from late January into late February, and fixes have to be requested inside that stretch. Call the assessor for this year's exact dates.

West Virginia Code 11-3-24 turns the county commission into a review panel, the board of equalization and review. They convene by February 1, may adjourn once February 15 has gone by, and must be done at month's end. An owner who never asks that panel for relief forfeits a correction for that year, though the Office of Tax Appeals remains open. After a hearing, the board's order can be appealed there, and the owner must meet a preponderance of the evidence.

Classification and taxability are outside the board's reach. A house you believe sits in the wrong class goes to the assessor as a separate protest under section 11-3-24a.

This break is limited to owners 65 or older and to owners who are permanently and totally disabled. West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 shields the first $20,000 of assessed value on an owner-occupied homestead, and the owner needs two years of state residency.

The home you lived in on the July 1 assessment date is the one that counts, and the savings begin the next tax year. A transfer by deed, will or any other route ends the break on the following July 1, unless the new owner meets the same tests. The assessor's site also links a Disabled Veteran Real Property Tax Credit form.

Back taxes will not block a closing, yet they must be settled before the deed is recorded. Here is the order that tends to work:

  • Have the sheriff's tax staff report on each ticket for the parcel, earlier years too.
  • Learn from the title company if the second list or a lien sale reaches the property.
  • Settle the balance from the sale check or ahead of closing, so no lien rides along with the deed.
  • Record the deed at the clerk's office and pay the transfer tax.

The transfer tax comes from West Virginia Code 11-22-2. It is $1.10 for each $500 of value, now retained by the county. A second county levy adds 55 cents per $500 unless the county raised it, and a $20 fee applies when the transfer is for consideration. The seller, as grantor, pays unless the buyer takes the deed with the tax still owing.

sections.h2: What a cash sale does and does not change
sections.html:
A cash buyer takes away the repair list, the open houses and the wait on someone else's mortgage approval. A tax lien stays put until someone pays it. Whichever way you sell, ask the sheriff's office for the tax status in writing before anything else. Bring your tax tickets, any deed you hold and, for an inherited house, the heir paperwork.

With an inherited house, the homestead exemption may already be gone, so the bill could run higher than what the last owner paid. Settle that with the sheriff before picking a closing date, since a title company will not close over an open ticket.

sections.h2: From first call to closing day
sections.html:
Picture a Raleigh County sale in four stages. Stage one is a call to the sheriff's tax desk at the courthouse for the balance on every ticket attached to the parcel. Stage two is a call to the assessor, since a rental or empty house is taxed at a heavier class than a home its owner lives in. Stage three is gathering papers: tickets, your deed, and any probate or heir documents.

Stage four starts once you accept an offer. A title search turns up liens and open tickets, and whatever it finds is paid out of your proceeds at closing. After that the deed is recorded with the county clerk and the transfer tax is paid. With a cash buyer the stages tend to go faster, since there is no lender adding appraisals or repair demands.

An older house may carry old deed wording and district names like the one noted earlier. Bring those up on day one and the file stays clean, with no surprise close to your closing date.

faqs.q: What are the due dates for Raleigh County tax bills?
faqs.a: One half is due September 1 and the other March 1. Early payment brings a 2.5 percent discount, and each half goes delinquent a month after its due date, on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my Raleigh County tax bill?
faqs.a: Walk in at the courthouse tax office in Beckley (304-255-9162), at the Ghent or Glen Daniel branch, or use the payment link on the sheriff's tax page. The branches shut for lunch from 12:00 to 1:00.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Raleigh County assessment?
faqs.a: See the assessor while assessments are open for inspection, then take any correction to the commission's review board before it closes in late February. Missing that session waives the correction for the year.

faqs.q: Can a Raleigh County house with delinquent taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from your proceeds or ahead of closing, and the title company can confirm the parcel is not on the list of delinquent liens certified to the Auditor each October 31.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Raleigh County sale?
faqs.a: Sellers do, as grantors, unless a buyer agrees to take the deed with the tax still owing. The basic charges are $1.10 plus 55 cents per $500 of value, with a $20 fee added, and a higher county rate is possible.
